# Deployment templates must project every behavior-binding clock — an unprojected inner timeout shipped blind on two successive plane generations

## Problem

The canonical provider-lane compose templates project some embed clocks (`NEO_OPENAI_COMPATIBLE_BATCH_EMBEDDING_TIMEOUT_MS`, probe timeouts) but not others — the contention ladder leaves (`NEO_OPENAI_COMPATIBLE_CONTENTION_TIMEOUT_MS`, `NEO_OPENAI_COMPATIBLE_CONTENTION_RETRY_COUNT`) bind **deadline-free interactive `embedText` calls** yet appear in no template. An operator reading the deployment file sees 300s/900s deadlines and cannot see the ~47s ladder that actually binds behavior. That invisibility shipped on two successive plane generations and was only found by live provider-activity trace.

Projection = the leaf is present in the template with its default, a plane-class guidance comment (CPU-constrained vs GPU), and parity-checked against the config source.

> **Scope wording corrected post-merge (see neomjs/neo#17125 debt 1).** This sentence originally read *"govern every single-input embed call"*, then *"the interactive `embedText` path"*. Both overstated it: bulk work routes through `embedTexts` under the batch ceiling, and **deadline-bearing probe calls bypass the ladder entirely** — neomjs/neo#17122 landed caller-owned probe deadlines, so a probe carries its own deadline rather than inheriting the ladder. Three successive narrowings of one sentence is itself the finding: a scope claim in operator-facing prose attracts overstatement, because the writer knows the mechanism and the reader only gets the sentence.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Canonical templates enumerate and project every clock in the **declared** `namespaces × clockSuffixes` profile, each with a plane-class guidance comment.
2. The config-leaf-parity gate (or a successor template lint) fails when a behavior-binding clock leaf exists in `ai/configBase.mjs` without template projection — mechanically, not by review discipline.
3. Existing planes' template deltas are enumerated in the PR body (which leaves become newly visible, with their effective current values unchanged).
4. ADR-0019 compliance throughout (no re-derivation, no hidden defaults in templates).

> **AC-1 wording corrected post-merge (see neomjs/neo#17125 debt 2).** It originally read *"every clock named by the ordering contract (the neomjs/neo#17114-class derivation table)"*. **#17114 closed NOT_PLANNED on 2026-08-14 without ever producing that table**, so the criterion was anchored to an artifact that will never exist. PR neomjs/neo#17117's body was corrected to own its declared set; this ticket was not, and a closed ticket stays discoverable — so the two disagreed with the more findable one being wrong. Coverage is what the declared profile says, and widening it is a reviewable policy edit rather than an appeal to a missing derivation.

## Contract Ledger

Added post-merge per neomjs/neo#17125 debt 2. Read from the shipped artifact (`$behaviorBindingProjection` in `ai/scripts/lint/config-leaf-parity.json` at `origin/dev`), not from the PR narrative.

| Target Surface | Source of Authority | Behavior | Failure Posture | Evidence |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `$behaviorBindingProjection.clockSuffixes` | `config-leaf-parity.json`, reviewed as a policy edit | Selects timing/retry leaves **mechanically** by suffix — no semantic judgment at lint time. Shipped set: `_CHUNK_SIZE`, `_KEEP_ALIVE`, `_RETRY_COUNT`, `_RETRY_DELAY_MS`, `_TIMEOUT_MS`, `_YIELD_MS` (6). | A leaf outside the suffix set is simply not in scope — silent by design, which is why widening is a deliberate edit and not a heuristic | `lint-config-template-ssot` suffix matching |
| `$behaviorBindingProjection.profiles[file].namespaces` | same | Bounds which env prefixes a given template is responsible for. Shipped: `NEO_OPENAI_COMPATIBLE_` (1 namespace, 1 profile). | Out-of-namespace env names are not demanded of that file | per-profile loop in `detectUnprojectedBehaviorBindingClocksFromSources` |
| Per-line projection shape | `classifyProjection` | A projected line must carry the canonical `# ENV: "value"  # guidance` shape, both token boundaries, a value **equal to the resolved config default**, and non-empty trailing guidance. | Four distinct violation codes rather than one: `unprojected-behavior-binding-clock`, `projection-default-mismatch`, `projection-missing-guidance`, plus the guidance-block count | mutation-tested in PR neomjs/neo#17117; a stale value, prose, or an `OLD_`-prefixed token each fail |
| Declared guidance-block count | `profiles[file].guidanceBlocks` | Prose blocks are counted, not inferred. Shipped: `3`. | Deleting a guidance block is a policy edit someone reviews, not a silent deletion — the per-line annotations alone once left this green | the count check, added after exactly that false green |
| Lint scan surface | `SCAN_SURFACE` | Declares `ai/deploy/**` alongside the `.mjs` roots, so the sibling parity spec **demands** the CI workflow watch it. | An undeclared read surface would let the spec report a satisfied invariant over an incomplete picture — the same shape as the unprojected clock these rules exist to catch, one layer up | `lint-guard-ci-parity` |

**Successor note.** PR neomjs/neo#17135 (#17121) widens this policy to 8 suffixes (`_PERCENT`, `_WINDOW_MS`), 3 namespaces (`NEO_MEMORY_SATURATION_`, `NEO_STORE_MEMORY_SATURATION_`) and 4 guidance blocks. The table above is the state **this** ticket shipped; the widening is recorded in that PR's own ledger.

## Evidence class

Template-vs-configBase diff (contention leaves absent from all templates) + the two-generation blind-ship history, 2026-08-14.

Part of epic neomjs/neo-agent-brain#38.

  prose that merely names the variable      (# ..._TIMEOUT_MS exists somewhere)
  a contaminated token                      (OLD_..._TIMEOUT_MS)

projection - which is the same operator-blindness this rule exists to end,
rebuilt one layer up inside its own fix.

The third slipped through because the earlier right-only boundary was justified
by reasoning about SHORTER-vs-LONGER generated names and never considered a
PREFIXED one. My own comment argued the left guard was unnecessary while leaving
that axis open.

Projection is now a canonical line: a COMMENT (never a live key, which is the
sibling rule's territory), both boundaries anchored, a value equal to one of the
leaf's resolved defaults, and a non-empty trailing guidance comment. Requiring
value-equality is what makes the documentation self-invalidating - change the
leaf and every stale comment fails on the next run.

Six red controls, one per false-green shape plus the live-key case. 61/61 green."

Projection is comment-only and deliberately so. Writing a default into compose
creates a second declaration site, which the config-leaf-parity gate already
bans as matches-config-default: a later change to the leaf would leave the file
silently pinning the old number. The comments carry the leaf name, its effective
default and plane-class guidance; uncommenting is then an explicit override,
which is the one case where a value belongs in compose.

The ladder is three leaves, not two. contentionRetryCount is a RETRY count, so
2 yields 3 attempts, and the total is 15000x3 + 1000x2 = 47000ms. Omitting
_RETRY_DELAY_MS would leave the 47s underivable from the file.

No live keys are added: the anchor still resolves to 17 keys and effective
values are unchanged."
- 2026-08-14T14:39:40Z @neo-opus-grace referenced in commit `4301178` - "feat(ai): fail the config lint on unprojected behavior-binding clocks (#17115)

The Compose/default parity rule bans a compose value that RESTATES a config
default, because a restated default is a second declaration site that silently
pins the old number when the leaf changes. Nothing banned the opposite failure:
a clock that binds real behavior and appears in the deployment file nowhere, so
an operator cannot see what governs the deployment.

This adds that inverse rule. One says do not duplicate the value; the other says
do not hide the knob. Together they leave exactly one declaration site and zero
invisible clocks. Projection is satisfied by a MENTION so the two rules stay
compatible: a commented line documents a clock without restating its default,
and the match runs against raw text because a YAML parse drops exactly the
comments that carry the documentation.

Scope is declared per profile rather than inferred. A blanket every-leaf rule
would flood a template with irrelevant knobs, and a noisy gate gets routed
around; each profile names the env namespaces it owns and the clock suffixes
select timing/retry leaves mechanically, with no semantic judgment at lint time.

The workflow gains ai/deploy/** because the rule scans compose templates and the
filters already state scanned-subset-of-watched. Without it, deleting a
projected clock would trigger nothing - the guard present, correct, and never
run, which is the class those filters call out twice.

Verified by mutation: removing the contention timeout from the template fails
the lint with the leaf named, and restoring it passes. 57/57 specs green."

The exemption mechanism mirrors forbiddenEnv -- one permits, one prohibits,
neither may be a bare list. An exemption is the one part of a guard that never
fails on its own, so a dormant one now fails: the key it names can be removed,
renamed, or drift off its default, and the entry would otherwise keep silently
licensing a restatement nobody decided on.

Its spec found a defect in it. Marking an exemption used on the env's mere
PRESENCE kept it alive for a key that had drifted to a genuine override --
nothing left to exempt, the entry immortal, and ready to permit the restatement
again if the value ever drifted back. It is now marked used only where it
actually suppresses a match.

* fix(ai): the chunk-size restatement is pinned for benchmark reproducibility, not accidental (#17125)

CI caught a wrong classification. #17125's table called
NEO_OPENAI_COMPATIBLE_BATCH_EMBEDDING_CHUNK_SIZE on provider-lane-worker "a
tuning knob, likely accidental" and I removed it. It has a consumer: the
provider-lane election benchmark compares embedding throughput across candidate
slot counts, and batch chunk size moves that throughput directly. A value
inherited from config would make runs taken either side of a config change
incomparable, with the drift invisible in the report --
ProviderLaneElectionRunner.spec.mjs asserts the pinned value, and
buildComposition reads the real YAML rather than a fixture.

Restored, and exempted with that reason. The verdict is now zero removed and
SEVEN exempted, which is the more interesting result: every literal restatement
in this file is deliberate. The rule's implicit premise -- that a second
declaration site is an accident -- does not hold for a deployment template at
all, and the profile's value is therefore coverage plus expiry rather than any
deletion: a future restatement fires, and the dormant-exemption check keeps all
seven honest.

Missed locally because I scoped the composition run to the lint directory the
diff touched. Four specs read this compose file; only one of them lives there.
All four now run: 332 + 140 green.

* fix(ai): an exemption must say why, and the keep-alive reason must match the topology (#17125)

Two findings from @neo-gpt-emmy's Round 1, and they are the same species as each other: a claim
that reads true until someone checks what it actually covers.

**The reason gate false-greened.** `Object.hasOwn` asked whether the exemption KEY existed and
never what it said, so `{NEO_MODEL: ''}` suppressed a real restatement. The comment three lines
above it already states the invariant — "an exemption that cannot say why it exists is
indistinguishable from the drift this rule catches" — so the prose carried the rule and the
check carried presence. The escape hatch false-greened on precisely the input its invariant was
written to refuse. Now a blank or non-string rationale is REPORTED as
`unreasoned-compose-default-exemption` rather than silently declined: quietly restoring the rule
would hide a malformed policy entry and send the operator to debug the restatement instead of
the exemption they thought they had written. It counts as used, so one defect yields one
violation rather than also tripping the dormancy rule.

**The keep-alive reason described a topology this profile does not have.** I wrote that `-1`

- 2026-08-25T15:41:43Z @dawesi referenced in commit `310359d` - "feat(ai): project every behavior-binding clock and gate the unprojected ones (#17115) (#17117)

* docs(ai): project embedding-lane behavior-binding clocks into the provider-lane template (#17115)

The contention ladder governs every single-input embed yet appeared in no
canonical template, so an operator reading the deployment file saw the outer
deadlines and could not see the ~47s clock that actually binds. It shipped
unprojected on two successive plane generations.

Projection is comment-only and deliberately so. Writing a default into compose
creates a second declaration site, which the config-leaf-parity gate already
bans as matches-config-default: a later change to the leaf would leave the file
silently pinning the old number. The comments carry the leaf name, its effective
default and plane-class guidance; uncommenting is then an explicit override,
which is the one case where a value belongs in compose.

The ladder is three leaves, not two. contentionRetryCount is a RETRY count, so
2 yields 3 attempts, and the total is 15000x3 + 1000x2 = 47000ms. Omitting
_RETRY_DELAY_MS would leave the 47s underivable from the file.

No live keys are added: the anchor still resolves to 17 keys and effective
values are unchanged.

* feat(ai): fail the config lint on unprojected behavior-binding clocks (#17115)

The Compose/default parity rule bans a compose value that RESTATES a config
default, because a restated default is a second declaration site that silently
pins the old number when the leaf changes. Nothing banned the opposite failure:
a clock that binds real behavior and appears in the deployment file nowhere, so
an operator cannot see what governs the deployment.

This adds that inverse rule. One says do not duplicate the value; the other says
do not hide the knob. Together they leave exactly one declaration site and zero
invisible clocks. Projection is satisfied by a MENTION so the two rules stay
compatible: a commented line documents a clock without restating its default,
and the match runs against raw text because a YAML parse drops exactly the
comments that carry the documentation.

Scope is declared per profile rather than inferred. A blanket every-leaf rule
would flood a template with irrelevant knobs, and a noisy gate gets routed
around; each profile names the env namespaces it owns and the clock suffixes
select timing/retry leaves mechanically, with no semantic judgment at lint time.

The workflow gains ai/deploy/** because the rule scans compose templates and the
filters already state scanned-subset-of-watched. Without it, deleting a
projected clock would trigger nothing - the guard present, correct, and never
run, which is the class those filters call out twice.

Verified by mutation: removing the contention timeout from the template fails
the lint with the leaf named, and restoring it passes. 57/57 specs green.

* fix(ai): declare the deploy-template scan surface so the watch is enforced (#17115)

The projection rule reads compose templates, but this lint's SCAN_SURFACE
declared only its .mjs roots. The sibling scanned-subset-of-watched spec takes
that export as authority, so it was asserting a satisfied invariant over an
incomplete picture of what the lint actually reads - and the ai/deploy watch
added alongside the rule was therefore unverified, correct by inspection only.

Declaring the deploy root makes the existing parity spec demand it. Verified by
mutation: removing the deploy filter from the pull_request trigger now fails
with "these scanned paths would not re-run the lint - the introducing PR lands
ungated", and restoring it passes 40/40.

This was the one seam left in the AC-2 claim. An undeclared scan surface is the
same defect as an unprojected clock, one layer up: the thing that governs is
real, the surface that should reveal it stays silent, and every downstream check
reports green over a picture that is missing a piece.

* fix(ai): validate the projection contract, not the presence of a name (#17115)

The first shape of this gate asked only whether an env NAME appeared anywhere in
the file. That proves an identifier is present and nothing about what an operator
reads, and three shapes passed it while publishing no usable information:

  a value that no longer matches the leaf   ("15000" after the default moved)
  prose that merely names the variable      (# ..._TIMEOUT_MS exists somewhere)
  a contaminated token                      (OLD_..._TIMEOUT_MS)

The middle one is the dangerous class. An operator trusts a number and only
distrusts a blank, so a projection that outlived its leaf is worse than no
projection - which is the same operator-blindness this rule exists to end,
rebuilt one layer up inside its own fix.

The third slipped through because the earlier right-only boundary was justified
by reasoning about SHORTER-vs-LONGER generated names and never considered a
PREFIXED one. My own comment argued the left guard was unnecessary while leaving
that axis open.

Projection is now a canonical line: a COMMENT (never a live key, which is the
sibling rule's territory), both boundaries anchored, a value equal to one of the
leaf's resolved defaults, and a non-empty trailing guidance comment. Requiring
value-equality is what makes the documentation self-invalidating - change the
leaf and every stale comment fails on the next run.

Six red controls, one per false-green shape plus the live-key case. 61/61 green.

* fix(ai): narrow the ladder's scope claim and enforce the guidance blocks (#17115)

Two truth gaps from cycle-2 review, both real.

1. The Compose comment claimed the ~47s ladder governs EVERY single-input embed.
It does not. chromaClientPrimitives routes bulk work through embedTexts in
sequential chunks under the batch ceiling, deliberately, so a fan-out cannot
storm a single local embedder into self-contention; the ladder governs the
interactive embedText path. Writing an overstated clock claim inside the fix for
overstated clock claims is the same defect one layer up, and the corrected
comment now names the scope and says why the bulk path is separate.

2. Deleting every prose guidance block left the gate green, because the per-line
trailing comment satisfied it. That annotation proves a line was annotated; it
cannot prove the file still explains what the knobs DO - visibility enforced
down to the identifier and the value, silent about the only part an operator
reads to decide. The expected block count is now DECLARED per profile, so
removing one is a reviewed policy edit rather than a silent deletion.

Rebased onto dev so the branch carries #17122's caller-owned probe deadlines.

Controls: removing one guidance block fails with the count named; the intact
tree passes. 62/62 green, compose parses, anchor still resolves to 17 keys."
- 2026-08-25T15:41:44Z @dawesi referenced in commit `e827182` - "fix(ai): put provider-lanes inside the parity rule, with exemptions that expire (#17125) (#17137)

* fix(ai): put provider-lanes inside the parity rule, with exemptions that expire (#17125)

Three operator-contract truth debts from the clock-projection gate.

1. The ladder scope claim, stated as a CONDITION rather than a caller list.
   It had been narrowed three times ("every single-input embed" -> "the
   interactive embedText path" -> ...) and was still wrong, because a caller
   supplying deadlineMs takes both halves of the ladder away in one branch:
   contentionRetriesLeft goes to 0 AND the per-attempt ceiling becomes the
   caller's deadline. A list of exempt callers rots the moment a caller is
   added, which is how the sentence kept drifting; the condition does not.

2. #17115's body dropped its universal "every clock" wording and its
   dependency on #17114, which closed NOT_PLANNED without ever producing the
   derivation table the criterion was anchored to, and gained the Contract
   Ledger it lacked. Ticket-side only.

3. provider-lanes.yml joins $composeDefaultParity. The ticket assumed three
   restated keys; measuring found SEVEN unique keys across four services --
   including NEO_OLLAMA_KEEP_ALIVE, the leaf this file's own guidance calls
   load-bearing for co-residency. So the verdict is split rather than uniform:
   the one key with no identity value is removed (it was already documented as
   a projection comment 200 lines above, so the file declared it twice), and
   six are exempted BY NAME AND REASON. Effective deployment values unchanged.

The exemption mechanism mirrors forbiddenEnv -- one permits, one prohibits,
neither may be a bare list. An exemption is the one part of a guard that never
fails on its own, so a dormant one now fails: the key it names can be removed,
renamed, or drift off its default, and the entry would otherwise keep silently
licensing a restatement nobody decided on.

Its spec found a defect in it. Marking an exemption used on the env's mere
PRESENCE kept it alive for a key that had drifted to a genuine override --
nothing left to exempt, the entry immortal, and ready to permit the restatement
again if the value ever drifted back. It is now marked used only where it
actually suppresses a match.

Resolves #17125

incomparable, with the drift invisible in the report --

buildComposition reads the real YAML rather than a fixture.

Restored, and exempted with that reason. The verdict is now zero removed and
SEVEN exempted, which is the more interesting result: every literal restatement
in this file is deliberate. The rule's implicit premise -- that a second
declaration site is an accident -- does not hold for a deployment template at
all, and the profile's value is therefore coverage plus expiry rather than any
deletion: a future restatement fires, and the dormant-exemption check keeps all
seven honest.

indistinguishable from the drift this rule catches" — so the prose carried the rule and the
check carried presence. The escape hatch false-greened on precisely the input its invariant was
written to refuse. Now a blank or non-string rationale is REPORTED as
